name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q01 - General formula exception for carbohydrates and non-carbohydrates

questiontext.text:
Which of the following pairs correctly identifies a compound that fits the general formula \(\mathrm{C}_x(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_y\) but is not a carbohydrate, and a compound that is a carbohydrate but does not fit this general formula, respectively?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा युग्म क्रमशः एक ऐसे यौगिक की पहचान करता है जो सामान्य सूत्र \(\mathrm{C}_x(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_y\) में सटीक बैठता है लेकिन कार्बोहाइड्रेट नहीं है, तथा एक ऐसे यौगिक की जो कार्बोहाइड्रेट है लेकिन इस सामान्य सूत्र में सटीक नहीं बैठता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Most carbohydrates historically were considered hydrates of carbon fitting the general formula \(\mathrm{C}_x(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_y\). However, this definition has clear exceptions where non-carbohydrates fit the formula and true carbohydrates do not.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
Acetic acid has the molecular formula \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}\) or \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{O}_2\), which can be written as \(\mathrm{C}_2(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2\). It fits the general formula but possesses carboxylic acid properties and lacks polyhydroxy aldehyde/ketone functionality, so it is not a carbohydrate. Conversely, rhamnose has the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_5\). It does not fit the ratio of carbon to water \(\mathrm{C}_x(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_y\), yet chemically it is a true carbohydrate (a deoxyhexose).

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Thus, the non-carbohydrate fitting the formula is acetic acid, and the carbohydrate not fitting the formula is rhamnose.

Final Conceptual Answer: Acetic acid and Rhamnose

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
ऐतिहासिक रूप से अधिकांश कार्बोहाइड्रेटों को कार्बन के हाइड्रेट माना जाता था जिनका सामान्य सूत्र \(\mathrm{C}_x(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_y\) होता है। हालांकि, इस परिभाषा के स्पष्ट अपवाद हैं जहाँ गैर-कार्बोहाइड्रेट इस सूत्र में फिट होते हैं और वास्तविक कार्बोहाइड्रेट इसमें फिट नहीं होते।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
एसिटिक अम्ल का आणविक सूत्र \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}\) अर्थात् \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{O}_2\) है, जिसे \(\mathrm{C}_2(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2\) के रूप में लिखा जा सकता है। यह सामान्य सूत्र में फिट होता है लेकिन कार्बोहाइड्रेट नहीं है। इसके विपरीत, रैम्नोज़ का आणविक सूत्र \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_5\) है, जो सामान्य सूत्र में फिट नहीं होता, फिर भी यह एक वास्तविक कार्बोहाइड्रेट है।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः सूत्र में फिट होने वाला गैर-कार्बोहाइड्रेट एसिटिक अम्ल है तथा सूत्र में फिट न होने वाला कार्बोहाइड्रेट रैम्नोज़ है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: Acetic acid and Rhamnose

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q02 - Definition and example of monosaccharides

questiontext.text:
A carbohydrate that cannot be hydrolysed further to give simpler units of polyhydroxy aldehyde or ketone is termed as a:

वह कार्बोहाइड्रेट जिसे पॉलीहाइड्रॉक्सी ऐल्डिहाइड या कीटोन की सरल इकाइयों में आगे जल-अपघटित नहीं किया जा सकता, क्या कहलाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Carbohydrates are classified on the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis into monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
A monosaccharide is the simplest carbohydrate unit that cannot be hydrolysed further into smaller polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. Oligosaccharides yield two to ten monosaccharide units upon hydrolysis, whereas polysaccharides yield a large number of monosaccharide units.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Therefore, the carbohydrate that cannot undergo further hydrolytic cleavage into simpler units is specifically a monosaccharide.

Final Conceptual Answer: Monosaccharide

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
कार्बोहाइड्रेटों को जल-अपघटन पर उनके व्यवहार के आधार पर मोनोसैकेराइड, ओलिगोसैकेराइड और पॉलीसैकेराइड में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
मोनोसैकेराइड वह सरलतम कार्बोहाइड्रेट इकाई है जिसे पॉलीहाइड्रॉक्सी ऐल्डिहाइड या कीटोन की सरल इकाइयों में आगे जल-अपघटित नहीं किया जा सकता है। ओलिगोसैकेराइड जल-अपघटन पर दो से दस इकाइयाँ देते हैं, जबकि पॉलीसैकेराइड अत्यधिक संख्या में इकाइयाँ देते हैं।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः जिस कार्बोहाइड्रेट का आगे जल-अपघटन नहीं हो सकता, वह मोनोसैकेराइड कहलाता है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: Monosaccharide

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q03 - Reducing ability of carbohydrates with Tollens reagent

questiontext.text:
Which of the following statements is strictly correct regarding reducing sugars?

अपचायी शर्करा (reducing sugars) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन पूर्णतः सही है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reducing sugars are carbohydrates capable of reducing Fehling's solution and Tollens' reagent due to the availability of free or potentially free aldehydic or ketonic carbonyl groups in solution.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, reduce Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution, making all monosaccharides reducing sugars. Polysaccharides are non-reducing, and sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide because its reducing groups (anomeric carbons) are engaged in glycosidic bond formation.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Hence, the correct principle is that all monosaccharides, regardless of whether they possess an aldose or ketose structure, act as reducing sugars.

Final Conceptual Answer: All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, are reducing sugars

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
अपचायी शर्करा वे कार्बोहाइड्रेट होते हैं जो फेहलिंग विलयन और टॉलेन अभिकर्मक को अपचयित करने में सक्षम होते हैं।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
सभी मोनोसैकेराइड, चाहे वे ऐल्डोज़ हों या कीटोज़, टॉलेन अभिकर्मक और फेहलिंग विलयन को अपचयित करते हैं, अतः सभी मोनोसैकेराइड अपचायी शर्करा होते हैं। पॉलीसैकेराइड अन-अपचायी होते हैं और सुक्रोज़ भी एक अन-अपचायी शर्करा है क्योंकि इसके अपचायी समूह ग्लाइकोसिडिक बंध में भाग लेते हैं।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः सही कथन यह है कि सभी मोनोसैकेराइड, चाहे ऐल्डोज़ हों या कीटोज़, अपचायी शर्करा होते हैं।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, are reducing sugars

answer.text: Only aldoses are reducing sugars, whereas ketoses are always non-reducing
Sucrose is a reducing sugar because it contains both glucose and fructose
All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, are reducing sugars
All polysaccharides are classified as reducing sugars

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q04 - Industrial preparation conditions of glucose from starch

questiontext.text:
Commercially, glucose is produced on a large scale by the hydrolysis of starch under which of the following specific reaction conditions?

व्यावसायिक स्तर पर स्टार्च के जल-अपघटन द्वारा ग्लूकोज़ का उत्पादन निम्नलिखित में से किन विशिष्ट अभिक्रिया परिस्थितियों में किया जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The industrial preparation of glucose involves the catalytic acid hydrolysis of polymeric starch into its constituent monomer units.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
According to industrial manufacturing methods, starch or cellulose is boiled with dilute sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)) at \(393\text{ K}\) under a pressure of \(2\text{--}3\text{ atm}\), yielding n moles of glucose:
\[(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_5)_n + n\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow[393\text{ K}, 2-3\text{ atm}]{\mathrm{H}^+} n\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6\]

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Therefore, the exact industrial conditions are boiling with dilute \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) at \(393\text{ K}\) under \(2\text{--}3\text{ atm}\) pressure.

Final Conceptual Answer: Boiling with dilute \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) at \(393\text{ K}\) under \(2\text{--}3\text{ atm}\) pressure

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
ग्लूकोज़ का व्यावसायिक उत्पादन बहुलक स्टार्च के उत्प्रेरकीय अम्ल जल-अपघटन द्वारा किया जाता है।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
व्यावसायिक विधि के अनुसार, स्टार्च को तनु सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)) के साथ \(393\text{ K}\) ताप तथा \(2\text{--}3\text{ atm}\) दाब पर उबाला जाता है, जिससे ग्लूकोज़ प्राप्त होता है:
\[(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_5)_n + n\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow[393\text{ K}, 2-3\text{ atm}]{\mathrm{H}^+} n\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6\]

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः सही व्यावसायिक परिस्थितियाँ तनु \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) के साथ \(393\text{ K}\) ताप और \(2\text{--}3\text{ atm}\) दाब पर उबालना हैं।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: Boiling with dilute \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) at \(393\text{ K}\) under \(2\text{--}3\text{ atm}\) pressure

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q05 - Reaction of glucose with prolonged heating with HI

questiontext.text:
When glucose is subjected to prolonged heating with hydroiodic acid (\(\mathrm{HI}\)), which hydrocarbon is formed as the final product?

जब ग्लूकोज़ को हाइड्रोआयोडिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) के साथ लंबे समय तक गर्म किया जाता है, तो अंतिम उत्पाद के रूप में कौन सा हाइड्रोकार्बन बनता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prolonged heating with hydroiodic acid (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) acts as a powerful reducing agent, converting all hydroxyl and carbonyl functional groups of a carbohydrate into hydrocarbons.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
When glucose (an aldohexose) is heated with \(\mathrm{HI}\) and red phosphorus, complete reduction of the six-carbon skeleton occurs without skeletal rearrangement:
\[\mathrm{CHO}-(\mathrm{CHOH})_4-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HI},\,\Delta} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3\]
The product is \(n\)-hexane, which confirmed that all six carbon atoms in glucose are linked in a continuous unbranched straight chain.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Thus, the resulting product is \(n\)-hexane.

Final Conceptual Answer: n-Hexane

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
हाइड्रोआयोडिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) के साथ लंबे समय तक गर्म करने पर यह एक प्रबल अपचायक के रूप में कार्य करता है और कार्बोहाइड्रेट के सभी प्रकार्यात्मक समूहों को हाइड्रोकार्बन में अपचयित कर देता है।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
जब ग्लूकोज़ को \(\mathrm{HI}\) के साथ गर्म किया जाता है, तो छह कार्बन वाली सीधी श्रृंखला बनती है:
\[\mathrm{CHO}-(\mathrm{CHOH})_4-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HI},\,\Delta} \mathrm{CH}_3-(\mathrm{CH}_2)_4-\mathrm{CH}_3\]
यह उत्पाद \(n\)-हेक्सेन है, जिससे यह सिद्ध हुआ कि ग्लूकोज़ के सभी छह कार्बन परमाणु एक सीधी श्रृंखला में जुड़े हैं।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः बनने वाला उत्पाद \(n\)-हेक्सेन है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: n-Hexane

answer.text: n-Hexane

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q06 - Chemical nature of the glycosidic linkage in disaccharides

questiontext.text:
The linkage connecting two monosaccharide units through an oxygen atom formed by the elimination of a water molecule is known as a:

जल के एक अणु के विलोपन द्वारा एक ऑक्सीजन परमाणु के माध्यम से दो मोनोसैकेराइड इकाइयों को जोड़ने वाला बंध क्या कहलाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In disaccharides and polysaccharides, individual monosaccharide rings are covalently joined via ether-like oxide bridges.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
The two monosaccharide units condense with the loss of a water molecule to create an oxide linkage (\(-\mathrm{O}-\)). This specific covalent linkage between two saccharide units through an oxygen atom is designated as a glycosidic linkage.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Hence, the linkage formed between monosaccharides through an oxygen atom is the glycosidic linkage.

Final Conceptual Answer: Glycosidic linkage

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
डाइसैकेराइडों और पॉलीसैकेराइडों में अलग-अलग मोनोसैकेराइड वलय सहसंयोजक ईथर-समान ऑक्साइड सेतु द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
दो मोनोसैकेराइड इकाइयाँ एक जल के अणु के निष्कासन द्वारा जुड़कर एक ऑक्साइड बंध (\(-\mathrm{O}-\)) बनाती हैं। ऑक्सीजन परमाणु के माध्यम से दो सैकेराइड इकाइयों के बीच बने इस विशिष्ट बंध को ग्लाइकोसिडिक बंध (लिंकेज) कहा जाता है।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः ऑक्सीजन परमाणु द्वारा दो मोनोसैकेराइडों को जोड़ने वाला बंध ग्लाइकोसिडिक लिंकेज है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: Glycosidic linkage

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q07 - Identification of non-reducing disaccharide sucrose

questiontext.text:
Among the following sugars, which one is classified as a non-reducing sugar?

निम्नलिखित शर्कराओं में से किसे अन-अपचायी शर्करा (non-reducing sugar) के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A sugar is non-reducing if its potential aldehydic or ketonic hemiacetal/hemiketal groups (anomeric carbons) are locked in glycosidic bond formation and cannot form an open chain in solution.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
In sucrose, the glycosidic bond is formed between \(\mathrm{C}_1\) of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose and \(\mathrm{C}_2\) of \(\beta\)-D-fructose. Since both anomeric carbons containing the reducing groups are involved in the bond, no free carbonyl group can be generated in solution. Consequently, sucrose does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagents and is non-reducing. In contrast, maltose, lactose, and glucose all contain free or potentially free hemiacetal groups at an anomeric carbon and act as reducing sugars.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Therefore, sucrose is the non-reducing sugar.

Final Conceptual Answer: Sucrose

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
यदि किसी शर्करा के एनोमेरिक कार्बन (ऐल्डिहाइड या कीटोन समूह) ग्लाइकोसिडिक बंध निर्माण में प्रयुक्त हो जाते हैं, तो वह अन-अपचायी शर्करा कहलाती है।

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
सुक्रोज़ में, ग्लाइकोसिडिक बंध \(\alpha\)-D-ग्लूकोज़ के \(\mathrm{C}_1\) और \(\beta\)-D-फ्रक्टोज़ के \(\mathrm{C}_2\) के बीच बनता है। चूँकि दोनों अपचायी समूह बंध बनाने में शामिल होते हैं, अतः विलयन में कोई मुक्त कार्बोनिल समूह उत्पन्न नहीं हो सकता, जिससे सुक्रोज़ अन-अपचायी शर्करा है। इसके विपरीत माल्टोज़, लैक्टोज़ और ग्लूकोज़ अपचायी शर्कराएँ हैं।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः सुक्रोज़ एक अन-अपचायी शर्करा है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: Sucrose

answer.text: Maltose

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q08 - Achiral naturally occurring amino acid glycine

questiontext.text:
Which of the following naturally occurring \(\alpha\)-amino acids is optically inactive due to the absence of a chiral carbon atom?

निम्नलिखित प्राकृतिक \(\alpha\)-ऐमीनो अम्लों में से कौन सा काइरल कार्बन परमाणु की अनुपस्थिति के कारण ध्रुवण अघूर्णक (optically inactive) होता है?

questiontext.text:
In aqueous solution, an amino acid exists predominantly as a dipolar ion known as a zwitterion. This species is formed because:

Amino acids contain both an acidic functional group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) and a basic functional group (\(-\mathrm{NH}_2\)) within the same molecule.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis

\[\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_3^+)-\mathrm{COO}^-\]
This resulting dipolar species carries equal positive and negative charges, making it overall electrically neutral. It is termed a zwitterion.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Hence, the zwitterion is generated when the carboxyl group loses a proton and the amino group accepts that proton.

Final Conceptual Answer: The carboxyl group loses a proton and the amino group accepts a proton within the same molecule

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
This reaction confirms that glucose exists in a cyclic hemiacetal structure where the \(\mathrm{C}_1\) position is locked upon acetylation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fructose is a ketohexose with a ketonic carbonyl group located at carbon-2 (\(\mathrm{C}_2\)) and primary alcoholic groups at \(\mathrm{C}_1\) and \(\mathrm{C}_6\).

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
In solution, D-(-)-fructose undergoes cyclic hemiketal formation through nucleophilic attack of the hydroxyl group at \(\mathrm{C}_5\) onto the ketonic carbonyl group (\(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)) at \(\mathrm{C}_2\). Thus, the ring is formed by the addition of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group at \(\mathrm{C}_5\) to the carbonyl group at \(\mathrm{C}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q16 - Optical rotation inversion during sucrose hydrolysis

questiontext.text:
Hydrolysis of dextrorotatory sucrose yields an equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-)-fructose. Why is the resulting hydrolysis mixture laevorotatory, giving rise to the term 'invert sugar'?

दक्षिणध्रुवण-घूर्णक सुक्रोज़ का जल-अपघटन D-(+)-ग्लूकोज़ और D-(-)-फ्रक्टोज़ का सममोलर मिश्रण देता है। परिणामी जल-अपघटन मिश्रण वामध्रुवण-घूर्णक (laevorotatory) क्यों होता है, जिसके कारण इसे 'अपवर्त शर्करा' (invert sugar) कहा जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Optical rotation of an equimolar mixture is the algebraic sum of the specific optical rotations of its individual components.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
Sucrose is naturally dextrorotatory (\([\alpha]_D > 0\)). Upon acid or enzymatic hydrolysis, it breaks down into an equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-)-fructose. The specific rotation of D-(+)-glucose is \(+52.5^\circ\), whereas that of D-(-)-fructose is \(-92.4^\circ\). Because the magnitude of laevorotation of fructose (\(92.4^\circ\)) significantly exceeds the dextrorotation of glucose (\(52.5^\circ\)), the net optical rotation of the resulting equimolar hydrolysate is negative (laevorotatory). This reversal in the sign of rotation from dextro (\(+\)) to laevo (\(-\)) is known as the inversion of cane sugar, and the mixture is termed invert sugar.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Hence, the mixture is laevorotatory because the laevorotation of D-(-)-fructose (\(-92.4^\circ\)) is numerically greater than the dextrorotation of D-(+)-glucose (\(+52.5^\circ\)).

Final Conceptual Answer: The laevorotation of D-(-)-fructose (-92.4 degrees) is greater in magnitude than the dextrorotation of D-(+)-glucose (+52.5 degrees)

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: The laevorotation of D-(-)-fructose (-92.4 degrees) is greater in magnitude than the dextrorotation of D-(+)-glucose (+52.5 degrees)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q17 - Monomer units and glycosidic linkage in maltose

questiontext.text:
Maltose is a reducing disaccharide. What are its constituent monosaccharide units and the nature of the glycosidic linkage holding them together?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A disaccharide's chemical behavior depends on the specific anomers of its monosaccharide monomers and the positions of the carbon atoms involved in the glycosidic linkage.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
Maltose is composed of two \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units. The glycosidic linkage is formed between Carbon-1 (\(\mathrm{C}_1\)) of the first glucose ring and Carbon-4 (\(\mathrm{C}_4\)) of the second glucose ring (an \(\alpha\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)4) glycosidic bond). Because \(\mathrm{C}_1\) of the second glucose unit remains as a free hemiacetal, it can open in solution to yield a free aldehyde group, rendering maltose a reducing sugar.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Therefore, maltose consists of two \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units joined by a \(\mathrm{C}_1-\mathrm{C}_4\) glycosidic linkage.

Final Conceptual Answer: Two alpha-D-glucose units joined by a C1-C4 glycosidic linkage

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
माल्टोज़ दो \(\alpha\)-D-ग्लूकोज़ इकाइयों से मिलकर बना होता है। इसमें पहली ग्लूकोज़ इकाई का \(\mathrm{C}_1\) दूसरी ग्लूकोज़ इकाई के \(\mathrm{C}_4\) से ग्लाइकोसिडिक बंध द्वारा जुड़ा होता है। दूसरी इकाई का \(\mathrm{C}_1\) हेमीऐसीटैल रूप में मुक्त रहता है, जिससे यह अपचायक गुण प्रदर्शित करता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q19 - Structural differences between amylose and amylopectin in starch

questiontext.text:
Starch consists of two polysaccharides, amylose and amylopectin. Which statement accurately compares their water solubility and structural branching?

स्टार्च दो पॉलीसैकेराइडों, एमाइलोज़ और एमाइलोपेक्टिन से मिलकर बना होता है। कौन सा कथन उनकी जल विलेयता और संरचनात्मक शाखन की सही तुलना करता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Starch is a polymeric blend of two structurally distinct components derived from \(\alpha\)-D-glucose: amylose and amylopectin.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
Amylose constitutes 15–20% of starch, is soluble in water, and consists of a long unbranched chain of 200–1000 \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose units held together solely by \(\mathrm{C}_1-\mathrm{C}_4\) glycosidic linkages. Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Therefore, amylose is water-soluble and unbranched (\(\mathrm{C}_1-\mathrm{C}_4\)), whereas amylopectin is water-insoluble with branches occurring at \(\mathrm{C}_1-\mathrm{C}_6\).

Final Conceptual Answer: Amylose is water-soluble with unbranched C1-C4 chains, whereas amylopectin is water-insoluble with branching occurring at C1-C6

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q22 - Classification of amino acids as acidic basic or neutral

questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amino acids are classified as acidic, basic, or neutral depending on the balance of carboxylic acid groups (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) and amino groups (\(-\mathrm{NH}_2\)).

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
- An equal number of amino and carboxyl groups results in a neutral amino acid (e.g., Alanine, Glycine, Valine).
- More carboxyl groups than amino groups make an amino acid acidic (e.g., Aspartic acid with side chain \(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{COOH}\) and Glutamic acid with side chain \(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{COOH}\)).
- More amino groups than carboxyl groups make an amino acid basic (e.g., Lysine with side chain \(-(\mathrm{CH}_2)_4-\mathrm{NH}_2\) and Arginine).

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Therefore, Aspartic acid is acidic and Lysine is basic.

Final Conceptual Answer: Aspartic acid (acidic) and Lysine (basic)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q24 - Chemical functional group nature of peptide linkage

questiontext.text:
Chemically, the peptide bond connecting two \(\alpha\)-amino acid residues in a protein is an:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Proteins are condensation polymers composed of \(\alpha\)-amino acid units linked sequentially via covalent peptide bonds.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
When the carboxyl group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) of one \(\alpha\)-amino acid reacts with the amino group (\(-\mathrm{NH}_2\)) of another, condensation occurs with the elimination of a molecule of water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)). The resulting covalent linkage has the structure \(-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}-\), which is an amide functional group. In biochemistry, this specific amide bond is designated as a peptide linkage or peptide bond.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Hence, the peptide bond is chemically an amide linkage formed between a \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) and an \(-\mathrm{NH}_2\) group.

Final Conceptual Answer: Amide linkage formed between a -COOH group and an -NH2 group with the loss of water

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q25 - Characteristics and examples of fibrous versus globular proteins

questiontext.text:

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Tertiary structure folding gives rise to two major molecular shapes in proteins: fibrous proteins and globular proteins.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
- Fibrous proteins: Polypeptide chains run parallel to one another and are held tightly together by intermolecular hydrogen and disulphide bonds, forming insoluble, fibre-like structural materials. Typical examples are keratin (present in hair, wool, silk) and myosin (in muscles).
- Globular proteins: Polypeptide chains coil around irregularly to produce compact spherical shapes. They are usually soluble in water; typical examples are insulin and albumins.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q26 - Primary structure of proteins and sequence variation consequence

What does the primary structure of a protein represent, and what is the consequence of altering this structure?

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q27 - Hydrogen bonding pattern in alpha helix protein structure

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q28 - Stabilizing non-covalent and covalent forces in tertiary protein structure

questiontext.text:
Which combination of chemical bonds and interactions stabilizes the tertiary (\(3^\circ\)) structure of proteins?

रासायनिक बंधों और अन्योन्यक्रियाओं का कौन सा संयोजन प्रोटीनों की तृतीयक (\(3^\circ\)) संरचना को स्थायित्व प्रदान करता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The tertiary structure of a protein represents the overall 3D folding of the secondary structure into compact globular or fibrous shapes.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
This complex tertiary folding brings distant amino acid residues together. Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Hence, the main stabilizing forces in tertiary structure are hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages, van der Waals forces, and electrostatic attractions.

Final Conceptual Answer: Hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages, van der Waals forces, and electrostatic forces of attraction

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q29 - Structural changes during denaturation of proteins

questiontext.text:
When a native protein undergoes denaturation due to changes in temperature or pH, which of its structural levels are disrupted and which structural level remains intact?

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Denaturation is the process by which a biological protein loses its unique three-dimensional conformation and biological activity without cleavage of covalent peptide bonds in the backbone.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
Physical changes (such as heating) or chemical changes (such as change in pH) disrupt non-covalent interactions like hydrogen bonds and salt bridges. As a consequence, globular domains unfold and helical structures uncoil, resulting in the loss of secondary and tertiary structural organization. However, the covalent peptide bonds forming the linear backbone are not hydrolysed under these conditions; therefore, the primary structure (amino acid sequence) remains intact.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Thus, during denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed, while the primary structure remains intact.

Final Conceptual Answer: Secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed, while the primary structure remains intact

चरण 2: विस्तृत विश्लेषण
तापमान या pH में परिवर्तन से हाइड्रोजन बंध व अन्य दुर्बल आकर्षण बल विक्षुब्ध हो जाते हैं। इसके कारण ग्लोब्यूल खुल जाते हैं और हेलिक्स अकुंडलित हो जाते हैं, जिससे द्वितीयक और तृतीयक संरचनाएं नष्ट हो जाती हैं। परंतु सहसंयोजक पेप्टाइड बंध नहीं टूटते, जिसके फलस्वरूप प्राथमिक संरचना अक्षुण्ण (सुरक्षित) बनी रहती है।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः विकृतीकरण के दौरान द्वितीयक और तृतीयक संरचनाएं नष्ट होती हैं जबकि प्राथमिक संरचना अक्षुण्ण रहती है।

questiontext.text:

How does a nucleotide structurally differ from a nucleoside in the architecture of nucleic acids?

questiontext.text:
In a polynucleotide chain of DNA or RNA, individual nucleotides are covalently connected through phosphodiester linkages between which carbon atoms of adjacent pentose sugars?

D-glucose has four chiral centres (carbons 2, 3, 4, and 5) in its open-chain Fischer projection, with the most oxidised carbon (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) drawn at the top.

Step 2: Assumptions and Rules
The configurational descriptors 'D' and 'L' represent relative spatial configuration compared to glyceraldehyde reference standards, and have no direct correlation with optical rotation sign \((+)\) or \((-)\).

Step 3: Relevant Principle
For monosaccharides with multiple asymmetric carbons, the configuration is assigned by examining only the lowest asymmetric carbon atom (the chiral carbon with the highest number, which is \(\mathrm{C}_5\) in aldohexoses).

The assignment is based solely on the right-hand position of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group at \(\mathrm{C}_5\).

questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Analyze open-chain glucose: \(\mathrm{CHO}-(\mathrm{CHOH})_4-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) versus cyclic \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose.

Step 2: Assumptions and Chiral Centre Definition
A carbon atom is asymmetric (chiral) if it is bonded to four chemically distinct groups.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
- In open-chain glucose: \(\mathrm{C}_1\) is \(-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{O}\) (\(\mathrm{sp}^2\), achiral). \(\mathrm{C}_6\) is \(-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) (two identical \(-\mathrm{H}\) atoms, achiral). Carbons \(\mathrm{C}_2, \mathrm{C}_3, \mathrm{C}_4,\) and \(\mathrm{C}_5\) each hold four distinct groups. Thus, there are 4 chiral carbons.
- In cyclic glucopyranose: \(\mathrm{C}_1\) becomes a hemiacetal carbon bonded to \(-\mathrm{H}\), \(-\mathrm{OH}\), \(-\mathrm{O}-\) (ring oxygen), and \(\mathrm{C}_2\). Because the two ring pathways starting from \(\mathrm{C}_1\) are non-identical, \(\mathrm{C}_1\) is asymmetric (the anomeric carbon). Carbons \(\mathrm{C}_2, \mathrm{C}_3, \mathrm{C}_4,\) and \(\mathrm{C}_5\) remain asymmetric, while \(\mathrm{C}_6\) remains achiral.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Total chiral centres in open-chain form = 4 (\(\mathrm{C}_2, \mathrm{C}_3, \mathrm{C}_4, \mathrm{C}_5\)).
Total chiral centres in cyclic pyranose form = 4 + 1 = 5 (\(\mathrm{C}_1, \mathrm{C}_2, \mathrm{C}_3, \mathrm{C}_4, \mathrm{C}_5\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The open-chain form contains 4 chiral carbons and the cyclic form contains 5 chiral carbons.

Final Conceptual Answer: 4 in the open-chain structure and 5 in the cyclic alpha-D-glucopyranose structure

questiontext.text:
Which of the following statements accurately characterizes the quaternary structure of proteins as exemplified by haemoglobin?

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Proteins composed of more than one polypeptide chain possess a fourth hierarchical level of organization termed quaternary structure.

Step 2: Detailed Analysis
Some biologically functional proteins consist of two or more polypeptide chains referred to as sub-units. The spatial arrangement of these individual folded subunits with respect to one another defines the quaternary structure of that protein. For instance, adult haemoglobin consists of four subunits (two identical \(\alpha\)-chains and two identical \(\beta\)-chains) arranged tetrahedrally into a cooperative tetrameric complex held together by non-covalent interactions.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q47 - Chemical mechanism of egg white coagulation upon boiling

questiontext.text:
Upon boiling an egg, the soluble white becomes an opaque, insoluble solid mass. What molecular change occurs during this process, and where does the physical water go?

अंडे को उबालने पर, उसका विलेय श्वेत भाग एक अपारदर्शी, अविलेय ठोस में परिवर्तित हो जाता है। इस प्रक्रिया के दौरान कौन सा आणविक परिवर्तन होता है, और इसमें उपस्थित जल कहाँ चला जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Phenomenon
Egg white contains soluble globular proteins (mainly ovalbumin) dissolved in water. Boiling causes coagulation and the apparent disappearance of liquid water.

Step 2: Underlying Principle
Thermal energy supplied during boiling disrupts the delicate network of hydrogen bonds and weak non-covalent forces stabilizing the native globular conformation.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Mechanism
- As temperature increases, the compact globular proteins unfold and the \(\alpha\)-helices uncoil (denaturation).
- The unfolded, exposed polypeptide chains aggregate and entangle, forming a three-dimensional insoluble matrix (coagulation).
- The large quantity of water present in the native egg white is absorbed and chemically/physically entrapped within the pores of this cross-linked coagulated protein network through extensive hydrogen bonding, rather than evaporating away.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Denaturation causes unfolding and coagulation of albumin, which entraps water within the gel matrix.

Final Conceptual Answer: Heat denatures globular albumin, uncoiling helices and unfolding globules into a cross-linked network that entraps and adsorbs water via hydrogen bonding

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q49 - Products obtained from complete hydrolysis of a thymine DNA nucleotide

questiontext.text:
What set of chemical products is obtained when a nucleotide derived from DNA containing the base thymine is subjected to complete hydrolysis?

थायमीन क्षारक युक्त DNA से प्राप्त न्यूक्लियोटाइड का पूर्ण जल-अपघटन करने पर रासायनिक उत्पादों का कौन सा समुच्चय प्राप्त होता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The reactant is a monomeric deoxyribonucleotide derived from DNA containing the pyrimidine base thymine.

Step 2: Principles of Nucleic Acid Composition
A nucleotide consists of three covalently bonded chemical components: a pentose sugar, a heterocyclic nitrogenous base, and a phosphate ester group.
In DNA, the pentose sugar is specifically \(\beta\)-D-2-deoxyribose (which lacks a hydroxyl group at \(\mathrm{C}_{2'}\)).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Hydrolysis
Complete hydrolysis cleaves:
1. The ester bond between the \(5'\)-hydroxyl and the phosphate group, releasing phosphoric acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\)).
2. The N-glycosidic bond connecting \(\mathrm{C}_{1'}\) of the sugar to the base, releasing free thymine.
3. The sugar core is released intact as \(\beta\)-D-2-deoxyribose.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The products are \(\beta\)-D-2-deoxyribose, phosphoric acid, and thymine.

Final Conceptual Answer: beta-D-2-deoxyribose, phosphoric acid, and thymine

चरण 2: न्यूक्लिक अम्ल संघटन का सिद्धांत
DNA में शर्करा इकाई \(\beta\)-D-2-डीऑक्सीराइबोज़ होती है। न्यूक्लियोटाइड में शर्करा, क्षारक और फॉस्फेट समूह उपस्थित होते हैं।

चरण 3: जल-अपघटन के उत्पाद

1. पेन्टोज़ शर्करा: \(\beta\)-D-2-डीऑक्सीराइबोज़
2. फॉस्फेट समूह: फॉस्फोरिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\))
3. नाइट्रोजनी क्षारक: थायमीन

अतः उत्पाद \(\beta\)-D-2-डीऑक्सीराइबोज़, फॉस्फोरिक अम्ल और थायमीन हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q50 - Structural implication of non-stoichiometric base ratios in RNA hydrolysis

questiontext.text:
When RNA is completely hydrolysed, there is no fixed stoichiometric relationship or 1:1 equivalence among the quantities of the four bases (A, U, G, C) obtained. What does this fundamental experimental fact indicate about the secondary structure of RNA?

जब RNA का पूर्ण जल-अपघटन किया जाता है, तो प्राप्त चारों क्षारकों (A, U, G, C) की मात्राओं के मध्य कोई निश्चित रससमीकरणमितीय (1:1) संबंध नहीं पाया जाता है। यह मूलभूत प्रायोगिक तथ्य RNA की द्वितीयक संरचना के बारे में क्या संकेत देता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Hydrolysis of double-stranded DNA yields bases where \(\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{T}\) and \(\mathrm{G} = \mathrm{C}\) (Chargaff's equivalence rules). However, hydrolysis of RNA reveals no quantitative equivalence among adenine, uracil, guanine, and cytosine (i.e., \(\mathrm{A} \neq \mathrm{U}\) and \(\mathrm{G} \neq \mathrm{C}\)).

Step 2: Principles of Base Pairing and Strandedness
In a complementary double helix (such as DNA), every purine base on one strand must pair via hydrogen bonds with a specific pyrimidine partner on the opposite strand (A with T via two H-bonds, G with C via three H-bonds), enforcing strict 1:1 molar ratios between base pairs.

Step 3: Deduction of RNA Secondary Structure
The absence of equimolar ratios among the four bases in RNA indicates that complementary base-pairing is not a global structural requirement. This proves that RNA exists naturally as a single-stranded molecule (which can fold back on itself irregularly, but does not possess an obligatory complementary second strand).

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The non-stoichiometric base ratios demonstrate that RNA is single-stranded.

Final Conceptual Answer: RNA is typically single-stranded and therefore does not require complementary base pairing throughout its structure

DNA के जल-अपघटन पर चारगाफ के नियम अनुसार \(\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{T}\) और \(\mathrm{G} = \mathrm{C}\) होता है, जबकि RNA के जल-अपघटन पर प्राप्त क्षारकों के बीच ऐसा कोई निश्चित 1:1 अनुपात नहीं मिलता।

चरण 2: पूरक क्षारक युग्मन का सिद्धांत

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
RNA में समानुपातिक संबंध का अभाव यह प्रमाणित करता है कि RNA मूल रूप से एकल-रज्जुक (single-stranded) होता है, जिसमें पूर्ण लंबाई में पूरक क्षारक युग्मन होना अनिवार्य नहीं है।

चरण 4: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
अतः यह तथ्य दर्शाता है कि RNA सामान्यतः एकल-रज्जुक होता है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: RNA is typically single-stranded and therefore does not require complementary base pairing throughout its structure

questiontext.text:
Malfunctioning of the adrenal cortex impairs the secretion of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids. Which clinical condition results from this adrenal cortex deficiency, and what are its characteristic physiological symptoms?

- Without hormone replacement therapy, this deficiency is fatal.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The disease resulting from adrenal cortex dysfunction is Addison's disease, characterized by hypoglycemia, weakness, and increased susceptibility to stress.

Thyroxine is a vital hormone produced by the thyroid gland. Chemically, it is an iodinated derivative of which amino acid, and what clinical conditions result from its abnormally low and high levels, respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Identify the chemical precursor amino acid of thyroxine and analyze the consequences of thyroid hormone dysregulation.

Step 2: Chemical Nature of Thyroxine
Thyroxine is synthesized in the thyroid gland by the iodination and coupling of the aromatic amino acid tyrosine. Hence, chemically it is an iodinated derivative of tyrosine.

Step 3: Pathophysiological Consequences
- Abnormally low levels of thyroxine lead to hypothyroidism, clinically characterized by lethargy, sluggish metabolism, and obesity. Dietary iodine deficiency can cause hypothyroidism accompanied by enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
- Conversely, an abnormally high or increased level of thyroxine causes hyperthyroidism, characterized by an accelerated metabolic rate.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of tyrosine; low levels cause hypothyroidism (lethargy and obesity) and high levels cause hyperthyroidism.

Final Conceptual Answer: It is an iodinated derivative of tyrosine; abnormally low levels cause hypothyroidism (lethargy and obesity), whereas elevated levels cause hyperthyroidism

चरण 3: असंतुलन के प्रभाव
- थायराक्सिन का असामान्य रूप से कम स्तर हाइपोथायरायडिज्म (अवथायरायडता) का कारण बनता है, जिसके मुख्य लक्षण सुस्ती (lethargy) और मोटापा (obesity) हैं। आहार में आयोडीन की कमी से थायरॉइड ग्रंथि बढ़ जाती है (घेंघा/गलगंड)।
- थायराक्सिन का बढ़ा हुआ स्तर हाइपरथायरायडिज्म (अतिथायरायडता) का कारण बनता है।

चरण 4: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
